newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia minister sees boom in oil and natgas.
newsitem.headline: Colombia minister sees boom in oil and natgas.

text.p: Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar said Thursday he hoped Colombia would be producing 920,000 barrels of oil per day by 1998, compared to current levels of 630,000.

Speaking to Colombia's National Association of Exporters, Villamizar forecast natural gas output could climb from its present level of 450 million cubic feet per day to 845 million cubic feet per day by 1997.
Villamizar said that within the next 50 years Colombia's proven reserves could increase from their current level of 3.5 billion barrels to more than 15 billion barrels.
And in his upbeat message to the nation's exporters, the energy chief predicted that within the next 10 years the value of oil revenue could be double the national budget.

But he tempered his comments, saying: What Colombia is looking at over the next few years isn't a bonanza like previos ones -- sporadic, ephemeral and ill-boding. The country is facing more and better prospects in terms of oil revenue. This is not a passsing bonanza but something that will last longer and requires a different approach.''
